summary: You developed a solid preliminary design for Great Barrier Reef monitoring, featuring well-chosen orbital parameters and effective STK access simulations. Your introduction articulated the Australian context and user base clearly. To improve, correct technical misconceptions regarding launch site kinematics for retrograde orbits, provide quantitative decay calculations for end-of-life deorbiting, and maintain professional presentation by replacing informal sources like Wikipedia and proofreading for incomplete sentences.
next_steps: Re-evaluate launch mechanics for retrograde sun-synchronous orbits (inclination ~97.8°), accounting for payload penalties and azimuth restrictions from equatorial versus high-latitude sites.
Perform quantitative orbital lifetime and drag-area calculations in the EOL section to mathematically prove compliance with the 25-year deorbit rule from 600 km.
Replace general sources and Wikipedia citations with peer-reviewed literature or official vehicle handbooks, ensuring all sentences and references are fully completed.

To reach Accomplished, ensure your launch site justification correctly accounts for retrograde inclination physics, fully detail required orbital maneuvers, and provide quantitative lifetime sizing for your drag sail.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion adequately recaps the primary architecture selections. To reach Accomplished, synthesize key quantitative design metrics—such as access durations, required delta-V, and calculated decay timelines—into your final summary rather than relying on qualitative statements.
